thread.title: Semi Stocks: Perfect Storm Brewing, Says Market Watcher

author: investopedia.com
title: Semi Stocks: Perfect Storm Brewing, Says Market Watcher
text:
Semi Stocks: Perfect Storm Brewing, Says Market Watcher By Shoshanna Delventhal | November 13, 2018 — 12:51 PM EST
The once red-hot semiconductor industry has been hit hard in 2018 amid broader market uncertainty and a wave of negative reports from analysts on the Street who are becoming increasingly bearish on sector fundamentals and a myriad of other headwinds. As losses continue into November, one market watcher sees more pain ahead for chip stocks. China Slowdown, US Market Saturation, Rising Rates, Trade Wars to Weigh on Chip Makers
In an interview with CNBC's "Trading Nation" on Monday, BK Asset Management managing director Boris Schlossberg said that the current environment is a "perfect storm for the semis at this point," signaling that the worst is yet to come.
"You have a slowdown in China, you have a saturation of demand in the Western markets, you have a rising interest rate environment, and you have the U.S.-Chinese trade war tensions which are putting pressure on prices," said Schlossberg.
New tariffs on Chinese imports are viewed as threatening supply chain costs for chip makers, already at risk of slowing demand for Apple Inc.'s ( AAPL ) iPhone and a broader maturation in the smartphone industry. On Monday, shares of semi stocks tumbled on a reduced outlook from Apple's Face ID supplier Lumentum Holdings Inc. ( LITE ), which cited a lower shipment request from a large customer.
"The general history of semis is they go from grossly overbought conditions to grossly oversold conditions, and I don't think we're anywhere near the capitulation point," said Schlossberg. "I think there's more to come to the downside before it finally washes out."
MKM Partner's chief market technician JC O'Hara chimed in on the CNBC segment, echoing the bearish sentiment.
O'Hara pointed to the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF ( SMH ), which fell 12% last month, marketing its weakest October performance to date.
"Coming into 2018, a pause was likely — that's following two years of 35 percent gains, so a pause or consolidation was actually healthy — but as this pause continued to draw out as the year progressed, we started to lose technical strength," he said, pointing to the chart.
O'Hara argued that if the SMH breaks below support at $86, which was the October low, "all bets are off." Trading Center
